title: Bonus or rebate?
hook: Would you spend the same $50 if its label changed?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Compare windfall and refund descriptions while holding available cash fixed.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Compare windfall and refund descriptions while holding available cash fixed.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy budget receives €50 and spends €22. How much remains, whatever the payment is called? Toy inputs A=[50, 22]; B=[50, 9.55].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[28, 22, 50], [40.45, 9.55, 50]]. Labels: Left €, Spent €, Total €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Both descriptions start with the same available cash. Different spending inputs change the remainder, not the payment itself. A label effect in a study concerns those choices, not a different budget identity.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Payment €=50, Spending €=9.55. What is Left €? Answer: 40.45.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Payment €=50, Spending €=9.55. What is Left €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 40.45. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: People spent more of a $50 payment framed as a "bonus" than one framed as a "rebate" ($22 vs $9.55) (Epley, Mak & Idson, 2006).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Compare windfall and refund descriptions while holding available cash fixed.
